title: AI isn’t close to curing cancer. This startup says it knows what it will take.
slides: Can AI cure cancer? This startup doubts it.
Most models fail because they predict, not explain.
Their approach: simulate every cell's molecular logic.
This changes which clinical trials you should join.
Ask if your trial uses mechanistic AI models.
thread_text:
1. Why AI won't cure cancer

Most models predict outcomes, but they don't explain the biology. That's why they fail in clinical trials.

2. The mechanistic twist

A startup is simulating every cell's molecular logic instead of just predicting. It's a different kind of AI.

3. The trial impact

This changes which clinical trials you should join. If a trial uses predictive AI only, you might be wasting your time.

4. The question for you

Ask your doctor: does this trial use mechanistic AI models? If not, consider alternatives.

5. Your move

Before you sign up for any trial, ask that one question. It could save you years of ineffective treatment.

instagram.caption:
Most cancer trials use AI that guesses your outcome—but can’t explain why. That’s a problem.

One startup is building models that simulate every cell’s molecular logic instead of just pattern-matching. They say this difference determines whether a trial wastes your time.

For you: before joining any trial, ask if it relies on mechanistic AI models. If not, you might be betting years on a black box.

Are you in a position to question your doctor’s trial choice—or would you just sign the form? 🧬⚗️🔬
